bib.title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Tables 26-28 (LLaMA-2 per-task zero-shot) not read in detail.

question: Can pretrained LLMs be pruned to high sparsity without retraining or second-order weight updates, using a cheap importance score?
hypothesis: Because LLMs have emergent large-magnitude input features, weight importance should combine weight magnitude with input activation norm, compared per output, which should beat magnitude pruning and match SparseGPT without weight update.
contributions: Wanda: pruning score |W_ij| * ||X_j||_2 compared per output row, no retraining and no weight update
Evaluation on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 (unstructured 50%, 4:8, 2:4) against magnitude pruning and SparseGPT
Analysis of fine-tuning, comparison groups, calibration size and weight update

method.summary: For each linear layer, score every weight by |W_ij| times the l2 norm of input feature j over calibration tokens, then zero the lowest-scoring s% of weights within each output row (or N:M groups). Layers are pruned in order, each seeing activations from the already pruned earlier layers, in one forward pass with no weight update.
method.task: post-training pruning of pretrained LLMs (unstructured and N:M sparsity)

datasets.name: C4 training set
datasets.split: random sample, same set as SparseGPT

datasets.name: EleutherAI LM Harness: BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OpenbookQA

inference.samples: Main tables use one fixed calibration set; Table 18 repeats over 5 random calibration seeds (mean, std).
inference.prompting: Zero-shot for 7 tasks; 5-shot for MMLU (following Touvron et al., 2023a).

parameters.calibration: 128 sequences from C4 train, context-length each (ablated 1 to 2048 in Table 17)
parameters.norm: l2 on input features; the paper says l2 works better than l1 and l-infinity
parameters.layers_pruned: all linear layers except first embedding layer and final classification head (about 99% of parameters), uniform sparsity

other.fine_tuning_lora: C4, auto-regressive loss, mask fixed, r=8 on query and value projections, about 0.06% extra parameters, 1 GPU and 12 hours
other.fine_tuning_full: C4, mask fixed, 4 GPU and 3 days
other.pruning_speed_hardware: NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, time for pruning metric only (excludes shared forward pass)
other.inference_speed: NVIDIA CUTLASS GEMM simulation on A6000, LLaMA-65B, batch size 1; end-to-end 1.24x on LLaMA-7B (251ms vs 312ms)
other.harness_commit: df3da98 on main; task version 0 except BoolQ version 1
other.fine_tuning_hyperparameters: learning rate, batch size, optimizer not stated in the text read

baselines: activation-pruning methods (mean, std, correlation, mean squared norm)
eval.protocol: One fixed calibration set for main results; 5 random seeds for robustness (Table 18); no significance test.

results.claim: Wanda at 50% unstructured sparsity on LLaMA-7B reaches WikiText perplexity far below magnitude pruning, without weight update.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, unstructured 50% sparsity, 128 C4 calibration sequences, no weight update; dense 5.68; SparseGPT 7.22
results.quote: for LLaMA-7B, Wanda is able to find sparse networks with a perplexity of 7.26, significantly better than the magnitude pruning baseline 17.29

results.claim: At 50% unstructured sparsity Wanda matches SparseGPT on LLaMA-2-70B perplexity.
results.table: Table 3, rows SparseGPT and Wanda 50%, column LLaMA-2 70B (3.98 both)

results.claim: Wanda at 2:4 on LLaMA-7B is worse than SparseGPT in perplexity.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 2:4 sparsity, no weight update vs SparseGPT
results.table: Table 3, row Wanda 2:4, column LLaMA 7B (11.53); SparseGPT 11.00
results.note: Paper: 'SparseGPT outperforms Wanda on 2:4 sparsity' on smaller models

results.claim: Mean zero-shot accuracy of 50% unstructured pruned LLaMA-7B with Wanda, versus dense.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 50% unstructured, no fine-tuning; SparseGPT 54.94; magnitude 46.94

results.claim: Gap to dense shrinks with scale: unstructured 50% LLaMA-65B and LLaMA-2-70B match dense zero-shot accuracy.
results.quote: unstructured 50% sparse LLaMA-65B and LLaMA-2-70B is able to match the zero-shot accuracies of their dense counterparts.
results.note: Table 2 gives 66.67 vs 66.97 for LLaMA-65B; the quote says 'match'

results.claim: Wanda pruning metric is hundreds of times faster to compute than SparseGPT's.
results.setup: LLaMA-65B, time to compute pruning metric across layers, NVIDIA A6000, excludes shared forward pass
results.table: Table 4, row Wanda, column 65B (5.6 s) vs SparseGPT 1353.4
results.note: Intro says 'can be 300 times faster'; 7B: 0.54 vs 203.1

results.claim: Structured 2:4 sparsity speeds up linear-layer matmul by about 1.6x on LLaMA-65B.
results.setup: LLaMA-65B, batch size 1, NVIDIA A6000, CUTLASS GEMM simulation; per layer 1.63x q/k/v/o, 1.61x up/gate, 1.54x down
results.quote: Structured 2:4 sparsity is able to bring notable inference speedup (around 1.6×) for linear layers in LLMs.

results.claim: End-to-end latency speedup for 2:4 sparse LLaMA-7B.
results.quote: For end to end latency, we observe a speedup of 1.24× on LLaMA-7B (251ms as compared to 312ms).

results.claim: Perplexity of LLaMA-7B at 70% unstructured sparsity without weight update is very poor; weight update helps a lot but still lags dense.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 70% unstructured, Wanda without weight update; with weight update 29.65
results.quote: where weight update can improve Wanda from 84.50 to 29.65

results.claim: At 80% sparsity Wanda collapses on LLaMA-7B and SparseGPT does much better, though both are far from dense.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 80% unstructured; SparseGPT 2e2; best 80% model (LLaMA-2-70B SparseGPT) 25.86

results.claim: Per-output comparison group gives best Wanda perplexity versus per-layer or other groups.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 50% unstructured; (output,1) 7.26 vs layer 7.95; magnitude metric per layer 17.29

results.claim: Wanda stays robust with very few calibration samples.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, 50% unstructured, one calibration sample; SparseGPT with 1 sample 10.22 (Table 17: Wanda 7.46 with 1)
results.quote: even with a single sample, pruned networks obtained by Wanda have a perplexity of 7.66
results.note: Sec 5 text says 7.66 with a single sample; Table 17 prints 7.46 for 1 sample

results.claim: Full-parameter dense fine-tuning recovers most of the zero-shot gap for 50% sparse LLaMA-7B.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B 50% unstructured Wanda, C4 fine-tuning, mask fixed, 4 GPU and 3 days; from 54.21
results.quote: could improve pruned LLaMA-7B from 54.21% to 58.15% in terms of zero-shot accuracy

results.claim: LoRA fine-tuning lifts 2:4 sparse LLaMA-7B above the unstructured 50% model.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B 2:4, LoRA r=8, 1 GPU and 12 hours, C4
results.quote: improves the zero-shot performance of structured 2:4 sparse LLaMA-7B from 48.53% to 54.46%

results.claim: Weight update gives no gain to Wanda at 50% and 4:8, small gain at 2:4.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B 2:4, Wanda with sequential weight update vs none

results.claim: Magnitude pruning collapses on OPT-13B at 20% sparsity while Wanda stays near dense.
5-shot MMLU: Wanda competitive with SparseGPT at 50% sparsity.

limits: Evaluated mainly on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 families; perplexity and 7 zero-shot tasks plus MMLU only.
Without fine-tuning there is a noticeable gap to dense; the gap is large at high sparsity (70%, 80%).
At 80% sparsity SparseGPT beats Wanda; authors suggest a small dense model may be better at extreme sparsity.
Speedups are measured as matmul simulation (65B) and end-to-end on 7B; not unique to Wanda.
On OPT, Wanda slightly underperforms SparseGPT; on small models SparseGPT is better at 2:4.
Per-output comparison advantage did not hold for image classifiers (layer-wise slightly better).
Fine-tuning budgets were limited (12 hours LoRA, 3 days full); authors say full recovery with more compute remains unknown.
Fine-tuning learning rate, optimizer and batch size are not stated in the text.

terms.definition: Pruning by Weights and activations: score |W_ij| * ||X_j||_2 compared per output
at most N out of every M contiguous weights to be non-zero

lineage.note: second-order pruning with weight update; Wanda's metric is a diagonal-Hessian simplification
emergent outlier features motivate the metric
